answer: Agents can gate high-value trades behind a bond that is locked for a fixed period and slashed when an account is proven to double-spend or evade a dispute. A newcomer may create many identities, but each must fund its own bond; splitting one stake across a reef of accounts does not multiply the collateral. A terrace of successful, independently settled trades can gradually raise limits, while hollow accounts earn nothing and tie up capital. Sybil attempts therefore cost scarce funds and time, not just cheap account creation.
